A living city district is not a settlement, an arena, a lane network or a traversal city, so the four segments took rows that each describe something else. This is the most forced part of the build and it is the part the whole prompt is about.

The asymmetry is invisible to the handoff. Two teams with different tools, speeds and objectives is the stated architecture, and spawn-teambase is the only field that can hold any of it - it says two bases, not two different spatial needs.

notes_for_us: Everything in this build came out of the reference, not the prompt. constraints/reference records that the user named a game, but there is no mechanism that says what the reference contains - the whole handoff is the intake agent's recall of one Roblox game, and nothing marks it as such for a reviewer.

genre-choice's step 1 says a brief prompt is not Unrecognised, and layout-intake says a named game is a theme statement. Both held here. What neither covers is that a named game also decides genre, shape and most options, which is far more weight than a theme.

A prison is a bounded institutional compound with interior blocks and a yard inside a wall. space-bounded describes the boundary and nothing else; settlement-static was the preset's shape and a prison is not a settlement. The same gap would hit a school, a hospital or a military base.

Roleplay's table has no perimeter wall and no exit gate, so both had to come from other genres via the catalogue. For a genre whose games are frequently enclosed institutions, that is a surprising pair to be missing.
